annotations.title: Find a workflow for a task

description: Sign-in required: call connect(email) and connect_verify first (free, one email) unless this connection is already signed in. For multi-step work, find a proposed method to compare with existing practice: checking whether a ruling or a provision still holds, a memo with sources, a matter digest, procedure and deadlines, what an article said on a date. The user's own workflows first, then Avokata's. Returns the best matches with why they fit, or that none fits and how to write one. Open the chosen one with get_workflow; to browse every workflow use list_workflows; to write a new one with the user use workflow_guide. Shipped plans are builder drafts, not professionally validated. Use, adapt, supplement or skip; a single lookup needs no setup. Cheap: no search is run and nothing is decided for the user. Example arguments: {"task": "ar dar galiu remtis šia nutartimi", "limit": 3}.

jurisdictions.description: Which jurisdictions to search, as codes. Held: `LT` (Lithuania), `EU` (European Union). Omit to search only the account's own; name every one the question needs. Keeps workflows written for the named jurisdictions and those written for none; omit for every workflow.
jurisdictions.title: Jurisdictions

limit.description: How many workflows to return, 1-5, default 3. The account's own come first, then the shipped ones, each with why it fits.
limit.title: Limit

session.description: The `session` value the sign-in returned. Pass it on every call in this conversation, so the sign-in survives however this client handles connections; omit it when the user connected with Sign in (OAuth) or a key.

task.description: The work you are about to do, in a sentence - in the user's words; Lithuanian matches best (`ar dar galiu remtis šia nutartimi`, `atmintinė su šaltiniais`).
task.title: Task
